nodes.label: React Compiler
nodes.rationale: Not enabled in this template because of its impact on dev & build performance.

nodes.label: Inline theme-detection script
nodes.rationale: Runs inline before first paint to read the stored theme preference (or resolve 'auto' via prefers-color-scheme) and set data-theme on the html element, avoiding a flash of the wrong theme (FOUC).

nodes.label: Collector (ingestion service)
nodes.rationale: Kept as its own process, separate from the Core Server, because ingestion is bursty, long-running, and horizontally scalable — a heavy backfill never degrades the chat API, and the two scale independently, communicating only over network/queue, never in-process.

nodes.label: MailConnector interface
nodes.rationale: Connectors sit behind a MailConnector interface so the orchestrator never imports a provider SDK directly; Microsoft Graph and Gmail integrations can drop in during Phase 1 without touching orchestration or tests. Current stubs return no messages so the whole pipeline runs end-to-end with no credentials.

nodes.label: DedupService
nodes.rationale: Keys on the immutable RFC Message-ID plus a content hash so re-runs never reprocess the same email; in-memory now, moving to a Postgres unique index in Phase 1.

nodes.label: Scheduler (interval, no overlap)
nodes.rationale: Runs incremental syncs on an interval and skips a tick if the previous run is still going, preventing overlapping/stacking sync runs.

nodes.label: Principle: The LLM is never the security boundary
nodes.norm_label: principle: the llm is never the security boundary

nodes.label: Principle: Design once for the product, switch on by tier
nodes.norm_label: principle: design once for the product, switch on by tier

nodes.label: Modular + layered (feature-first) pattern
nodes.rationale: Technical-only folders (controllers/, models/) don't scale, and full DDD/hexagonal is overkill here; feature-modules let a new developer copy modules/users/ as the template for any new domain (auth, org, mailbox, chat, audit, ...).

nodes.label: Drizzle ORM (PostgreSQL)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for the project's SQL-heavy needs — recursive-CTE reporting-chain permissions, row-level security, JSONB, append-only audit — plus a small on-prem footprint.

nodes.label: UserRepository interface (in-memory/Postgres swap)
nodes.rationale: createUserRepository() swaps an in-memory store (NODE_ENV=test or DB_DRIVER=memory) for the PostgreSQL repository behind the same interface, so service and controller code is identical either way and tests run without a database.

nodes.label: RAG Email Attachment Ingestion Pipeline (test/sample data)
nodes.norm_label: rag email attachment ingestion pipeline (test/sample data)

nodes.label: Incremental ingestion cursor / fail-safe retry design
nodes.rationale: If any message fails during a run, the sync cursor is not advanced at all; the next run retries the whole window from the same starting point. This is safe because re-ingesting an already-succeeded message just overwrites its Qdrant points rather than duplicating them.
nodes.norm_label: incremental ingestion cursor / fail-safe retry design

nodes.label: Thread-pool concurrency tied to OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL
nodes.rationale: Each email's chunk->embed->upsert step runs in a thread pool because the work is I/O-bound (HTTP calls to Ollama + Qdrant), so the GIL is released and threads give real speedup. Going much above Ollama's own OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL (default 4) just queues requests on Ollama's side without extra throughput, so --workers rarely needs to exceed that.

nodes.label: RBAC filtering enforced inside the Qdrant query
nodes.rationale: Filtering happens inside the Qdrant query itself, so restricted chunks never leave the vector store, let alone reach the LLM -- access control is enforced structurally rather than trusted at the prompt/LLM layer.
nodes.norm_label: rbac filtering enforced inside the qdrant query

nodes.label: No SQLite fallback -- Postgres-only backend
nodes.rationale: Postgres is the only backend this system talks to, so pointing POSTGRES_URL at the Core Server's real database is not optional -- there is no lightweight local fallback path.

nodes.label: unstructured + Apache Tika / PaddleOCR (target parsing/OCR stack)

nodes.label: Flagship example: CEO proposal + summary query
nodes.norm_label: flagship example: ceo proposal + summary query

nodes.label: Privacy-first / on-prem design principle
nodes.rationale: No mail ever leaves the customer perimeter; the LLM runs locally on a dedicated AI node (MiPhi chip), self-hosted, with no cloud LLM APIs -- driven by enterprise data-sovereignty requirements.

nodes.label: RAG, not training -- design principle
nodes.rationale: Knowledge lives in a vector database and is retrieved at query time, never baked into model weights, so it stays fresh, auditable, and deletable -- a trade-off favoring governance/compliance over fine-tuning.

nodes.label: Hierarchy-gated access -- enforced outside the model
nodes.rationale: A manager can see their reports' mail, peers are isolated, the CEO sees everything -- enforced outside the model, in the database, so the LLM is never trusted as the access-control boundary.
nodes.norm_label: hierarchy-gated access -- enforced outside the model

nodes.label: Grounded answers -- strictly source-backed, always cited
nodes.rationale: Answers are strictly source-backed and always cited, returning 'not found' when unsupported -- prioritizing auditability and trust over answer coverage.
nodes.norm_label: grounded answers -- strictly source-backed, always cited
